Bhāmatī
------------------------------------------
The philosophy of the उपनिषद्स् has been systematized in the Brahmasūtras (also called the Vedāntasūtras) attributed to बादरायण. The Hindu tradition identi-fies him with the व्यास of the Mahā-bhārata fame.
Of the several Sanskrit commentaries on it extant today, शङ्कर’s (A.

-820) is the earliest. In the post-शङ्कर period, several sub-commentaries were written on his Brahmasūtra-bhāṣya, necessitated by the need to further amplify certain subtle points of the Advaita philosophy or to counter the dialectical criticisms against the school. One of the most outstanding of these, is the Bhāmatī of वाचस्पति मिश्र (9th century A. D.) which created a new sub-school of Advaita Vedānta, known as the Bhāmatī Prasthāna.
The story goes that वाचस्पति मिश्र named his celebrated gloss after his wife भामती who had served him devotedly, sacrificing all the conjugal pleasures, so that he could totally apply his मिन्द् to the creative literary work.
The Bhāmatī, again, has six commentaries on it, the best-known among them being the Kalpataru of Amalānanda (13th century A. D.)
The views of the भामती school can be briefly summarised as follows: ब्रह्मन् is the material cause of this world, not as the locus of अविद्या or nescience but as the object of avidyās supported by the jīvas or individual selves. Māyā is only an accessory cause. अविद्या cannot abide in ब्रह्मन्. It abides in the jīvas and is plural. वाचस्पति advocates two kinds of avidyās: the मूलाविद्या or kāraṇāvidyā (primal nescience) and the tūlāvidyā or kāryāvidyā (derivative nescience). It is the latter that is responsible for error impressions. Also, वाचस्पति seems to be more inclined towards the ‘avaccheda-वाद’ or the theory of limitation with regard to the appearance of the jīvas. Just as a pot limits the infinite sky in itself, अविद्या of the individual limits ब्रह्मन् and makes it appear like a जीव. Another point of importance of this work is that the महावाक्यस् or great sentences (like tat tvam asi) do not produce anubhava or immediate experience. It is the मिन्द् seasoned by meditation that gives such experience.
See also ADVAITA VEDĀNTA DARŚANA and VĀCASPATI MIŚRA.
